chunks.text: Name: Vimal Desai Title: Sr. Full-Stack Engineer Tagline: I build products people actually use — React, Node, TypeScript, and the seams between them. Bio: Full-stack engineer, 10+ years. React, Node, TypeScript. Right now at UpKeep I ship CMMS features, in-product AI, and an internal factory that turns tickets into reviewed PRs. Location: Surat, Gujarat, India (Asia/Kolkata) Work: remote, full-time. Strong preference for remote. Can provide 4–5 hours of daily overlap with any time zone. Relocation: Would require visa sponsorship for international relocation. Email: vimlesai@duck.com Preferred contact: email Site: https://vimlesai.io Links: GitHub: https://github.com/VimLeSai · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/vimlesai · Upwork: https://www.upwork.com/freelancers/vimlesai · npm: https://www.npmjs.com/~vimlesai · Stack Overflow: https://stackoverflow.com/users/7801396/vimlesai · vimlesai.io: https://vimlesai.io/ · Contra: https://contra.com/VimLeSai/about · Toptal: https://www.toptal.com/resume/vimal-desai · Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/vimlesai/ Now at UpKeep: CMMS features, in-product AI, ticket-to-PR factory. Public language only — no internal product or ticket names.

I started in UI because that's where users feel the product. Backend work followed because that's where it breaks. Since 2018 I've shipped ERPs, CRMs, travel flows, and a lot of unglamorous production software. Led teams, ran interviews, handed work to people who could keep it. At UpKeep I work across web, APIs, and shared services — vendor and parts, event pipelines, in-product AI, and a ticket-to-PR factory. Same habit: understand the problem, keep the seams clean, don't merge without tests.
Languages: Gujarati (native), Hindi (native), English (professional)
B.Sc. Computer Science in Computer Science — Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan University, Bhopal, MP, India. 2015–2018.
AI & Emerging Tech: Agent-assisted delivery loops, evals, and in-product AI. Still the person who reviews what merges.
Hackathons: Enjoy time-boxed problem solving and rapid prototyping — secured 3rd place in an internal AI hackathon at UpKeep.
Open Source: Building and sharing reusable tools and components on GitHub.
Chess: Strategic thinking on and off the board.
Table Tennis: Quick reflexes — useful in both ping-pong and production incidents.
Video Production: Produced event videos for college festivals during early career at Codelash.
Graphic Design: Designed promotional materials and posters in early career; still enjoy visual design.
Quote: "I've always wanted to simplify things more than they already are. Making everything simpler for users is what ultimately inspires me to work." — On what drives my engineering philosophy
Sr. Software Engineer at UpKeep. November 2023 – Present. Remote, India. Current role.
UpKeep — Full-Stack CMMS Delivery: Most tickets touch more than one repo — web, APIs, sometimes an event path. Vendor and parts, webhooks, everyday CMMS UI.
UpKeep — AI Product Engineering: In-product AI: who gets access, how credits work, how output gets scored, and a board for humans to review it.
UpKeep — Agent-Assisted Delivery: Internal ticket-to-PR factory — intake, implementation, review, QA. On factory weeks that’s typically 5–8 PRs a day. I still review what merges.
UpKeep — QA & Review: Test plans and Playwright sit in the same loop as the PR. Review isn’t a ceremony after shipping.
UpKeep — Preventive Maintenance & Releases: Earlier: a lot of time in Preventive Maintenance, and a stretch owning platform releases with no downtime window.
UpKeep — Recognition: Leader of the Month twice. 3rd in an internal AI hackathon for a data-consistency POC.
Skills used at UpKeep: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Angular, Node.js, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Express, tRPC, Apache Kafka, Docker, Cypress, Playwright, Jest, Amazon SNS
Sr. Software Development Engineer at Emtec Inc.. September 2022 – November 2023. Remote, India.
Emtec Inc. — Rental platform UI: Built the web app for a US rental platform — React, Next.js, TypeScript — with Cypress and Jest covering the paths that actually broke.
Emtec Inc. — APIs: Owned NestJS services on MongoDB and PostgreSQL. GraphQL where the UI needed it, REST everywhere else.
Emtec Inc. — Test pipelines: Cut the wait on automated tests with Cypress, k6, and JMeter so releases didn’t sit in a queue.
Emtec Inc. — Working with the CTO: Sat with engineering leadership on the features that had to hold under load. Coding standards work later showed up as about an 11% efficiency gain.
Skills used at Emtec Inc.: React, Next.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, GraphQL, Apache Kafka, Docker, Cypress, Jest
Tech Lead & Sr. Front-End Developer at Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.. June 2018 – July 2022. Surat, Gujarat, India.
Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — StringERP: Built StringERP from scratch — React, Node, TypeScript. Modular frontend, services behind it, releases every couple of weeks.
Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — Implr: Split one module out as its own product. Same codebase habits, its own deploy.
Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — Intern → Tech Lead: Four years, intern to Tech Lead. 50+ projects across textiles, healthcare, travel, real estate, and a few others.
Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — The team: Ran a mixed team of 11–20 — frontend, backend, Flutter, BAs. Interviews (40+ frontend), sprints, client calls, deploys.
Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — Module kit: Reusable frontend modules so a new domain didn’t take days of wiring. New ones landed in under 10 minutes.
Skills used at Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.: React, Next.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, Node.js, MongoDB, Tailwind CSS, Redux, Angular, jQuery, Vite, Laravel, AWS, Docker, RabbitMQ, SCSS / SASS
Java Intern at Croods Consolidate. April 2018 – June 2018. Vadodara, Gujarat, India.
Croods Consolidate — Internship: Three-month Java intern. Core Java and JSP — the first job that wasn’t HTML.
Skills used at Croods Consolidate: Java
Web Developer at Codelash. April 2017 – May 2018. Vadodara, Gujarat, India.
Codelash — Websites: Client sites in HTML, CSS, SASS, PHP, and JavaScript. First time shipping for someone who wasn’t me.
Codelash — The startup: Helped the CEO with the in-house product and the unglamorous offline marketing that came with a college-born shop.
Codelash — Posters and video: Festival posters, and video for MSU events — Paramarsh, Junoon, Footprints, Prerna.
Skills used at Codelash: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, SCSS / SASS, LESS, PHP, jQuery

StringERP (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Textile ERP I built from scratch — ledgers, orders, inventory, and a module kit. Lead Architect & Full-Stack Engineer StringERP is a textile ERP I built from zero — marketing site, the product, and Implr as a spin-out. Ledgers, purchase and sales orders, inventory. Thousands of transactions a day. Releases every two weeks. New modules went from days of wiring to under 10 minutes. Concurrent order edits stopped corrupting rows after we put MongoDB transactions and locks on the writes. URL: https://www.stringerp.com/ Tags: Enterprise SaaS, ERP, CRM

StringERP — Two people, one order: As the client grew, two people would edit the same purchase or sales order at once. Rows went stale or wrong. MongoDB transactions and distributed locks made those writes atomic.
StringERP — CSV dumps: Clients needed to import legacy Excel/CSV without taking the app down. A RabbitMQ queue processed uploads one at a time and emailed when they finished.
StringERP — New modules took days: Adding a domain meant wiring folders by hand. I made a copy-paste module shape so a new one landed in under 10 minutes.

Mastery Logistics System (Emtec Inc.) Logistics TMS — I moved production from MySQL to PostgreSQL without taking the site down. Full-Stack Engineer Mastery Cloud TMS is a logistics platform that has to stay up. I did frontend work in TypeScript and Redux Toolkit, NestJS APIs, and the MySQL → PostgreSQL move while customers were still using the product. Moved production logistics data MySQL → PostgreSQL with a TypeScript script that compared both sides live. No hand-checking thousands of rows. Nothing dropped. URL: https://www.mastery.net/ Tags: Logistics, SaaS, TMS, Database Migration
Mastery Logistics System — Move the database, keep the site up: Production logistics data, MySQL to PostgreSQL, no downtime window. Both databases had to be true at the same time until cutover.
Mastery Logistics System — Nobody can eyeball thousands of rows: Manual QA before cutover wasn’t a plan. We needed a script that told us what didn’t match.
Mastery Logistics System — APIs under load: P90 latency had a number attached. NestJS endpoints needed JMeter, not hope.

RentBase (Emtec Inc.) US rental leads CRM — portal, NestJS API, TransUnion screening, and marketing site for a 3-person team. Senior Full-Stack Engineer RentBase connects landlords, agents, and renters around listings and lead qualification. Lean 3-person core team; I worked directly with the CEO (ex-Zillow lead). Owned the React/TypeScript portal, built NestJS modules for screening and related domain APIs, and helped keep the marketing site and admin panel in sync with product reality. Cut manual QA on multi-role flows by ~70% with Postman lifecycle scripts. Shipped TransUnion screening end-to-end so agents could run credit/background checks inside the product instead of juggling vendor portals. Tags: Real Estate, CRM, PropTech, Startup
RentBase — No QA seat: Onboarding spans agent → landlord → listing → renter → screening report. Manual regression before every deploy was eating the whole week.

RentBase — TransUnion screening: PII-heavy flow: shareable landlord/property records, renter validation exams, status/delivery webhooks, IP-guarded notification endpoints, and report UI that agents actually trust.
RentBase — Many surfaces, one product: Portal, Nest API, admin, and Next.js marketing site had to stay consistent for leads, listings, follow-ups, and HubSpot sync without a large platform team.

Africa Business Console (Emtec Inc.) ETK's first product — React + NestJS so a new country was config, not a rewrite. Senior Full-Stack Engineer ETK needed a first product for companies doing business in and out of Africa. I built the console — React, TypeScript, NestJS — knowing rules and currencies would change by country. ETK's first digital product. I put the component kit and folder rules in place so the next country didn't mean a rewrite. Tags: Enterprise, Cross-Border Operations, Dashboard
Africa Business Console — Every country is a little different: Currency, compliance, paperwork. The UI had to bend without a fork per market.
Africa Business Console — First product, so the habits stick: Whatever we put in the repo would be the template. Folder layout and components had to be copyable.

UpKeep Platform (UpKeep) Full-stack CMMS delivery, in-product AI, and an internal ticket-to-PR factory. Sr. Software Engineer UpKeep is a mobile-first CMMS and asset operations platform. As a Sr. Software Engineer I ship full-stack tickets across web, APIs, and shared services — vendor and parts workflows, event pipelines, in-product AI, and an internal factory that turns tickets into reviewed PRs. Earlier work includes the Preventive Maintenance module and a stretch as Release Engineer. On factory weeks, typically 5–8 reviewed PRs a day. Earlier: sprint velocity 16 → 40+ story points; Leader of the Month (2×); 3rd place in an internal AI hackathon. URL: https://www.upkeep.com/ Tags: CMMS, Enterprise SaaS, AI Product, Agent Delivery

UpKeep Platform — Work spans more than one repo: A typical ticket touches UI, API routes, and sometimes an event consumer. The job is to keep those changes consistent without leaking unfinished work across services.

UpKeep Platform — AI features need product rails, not demos: In-product AI needs access control, credits, scoring, and a place for humans to review output. Shipping the model call is the easy part; the rails around it are the work.

UpKeep Platform — Speed without skipping the loop: An internal factory can draft a lot of PRs. The constraint is keeping review, Playwright, and merge hygiene attached so volume does not become noise.

Micqro (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Quiz-first social app — typed polls in the feed, chat, campaigns, and EC2/pm2 deploys. Frontend Engineer Micqro (codebase lived under affy-frontend) is a quiz-first social product. Posts are polls and questions; the feed shows how people answered. Built the Next.js client end-to-end: auth, feed, poll composer, chat, search, profiles, notifications, and campaign surfaces, then wired EC2/pm2 deploys. Shipped a social feed where the unit of content is a question — with answer distributions inline — plus DMs and campaigns, not another photo wall. Tags: Social Media, Quizzes, Community
Micqro — Many poll shapes, one feed: Star rating, currency, date-time, short/long text, and choice polls each need distinct composers and result UIs without turning the feed into a mess.
Micqro — Social chrome on top of quizzes: Mentions, media cropping, chat attachments, saved posts, and interest tags had to feel native next to analytics in the same scroll.

(not)Loco Therapy site from Figma — calm type and spacing, not a clinic brochure. UI Design & Development (not)Loco connects people with licensed therapists over voice notes and video. I took the Figma and built the site. The brief was: don’t look clinical, don’t look loud. A therapy marketing site that doesn’t look like a clinic brochure. Figma → Next.js + Tailwind, with type and spacing doing the work. Tags: Healthcare, Mental Health, UI Design, Marketing Site
(not)Loco — Tone: People arriving here are not shopping. Type, space, and color had to feel quiet without going cold.

Rampnow Sole frontend engineer on a global payment platform — four modules, one engineer. Sole Frontend Engineer Rampnow lets merchants take payments. I was the only frontend person. Four surfaces — public site, checkout widget, merchant console, internal admin — from wireframes to live APIs. Four UIs, one frontend engineer: landing page, checkout widget, merchant dashboard, admin. Wired to live payment APIs and webhooks. Tags: Fintech, Payments, Admin Console, Dashboard
Rampnow — Four UIs, one of me: Visitor, customer, merchant, admin. Different APIs, different permissions, same calendar.
Rampnow — Payments fail in the edges: Gateway APIs, hosted checkout, webhooks. Most of the work was the states between “pay” and “paid”.

Textile Aadhar (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Zari, thread, and yarn shop — homepage and products come from the admin, not a deploy. Full-Stack Engineer Store for Zari, threads, and yarn. Shop plus admin. The homepage, which categories showed, and which fields a product had — all from the admin, not a deploy. First time I owned the whole thing. First project I ran end to end. Admin could change the landing page, categories, and product fields without a deploy. Also the project that taught me to check before you ship. URL: https://www.textileaadhar.com/ Tags: Textiles, E-commerce, Admin Panel
Textile Aadhar — Admin owns the homepage: Layout, categories, product fields. If the client wanted a new block, it couldn’t wait on me.

Textile ERP (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Mill ERP — designs, recipes, warp/weft math, inventory, orders. The formulas had to match the floor. Frontend Engineer ERP for a fabric mill: designs, recipes (the cloth pattern), warp and weft calculations, manufacturing, inventory, sales and purchase orders. Textile ERP from design recipes through warp/weft math, inventory, and sales. The formulas came from sitting with the mill, not from a spec. Tags: Textiles, ERP, Admin Panel
Textile ERP — The math is the product: Warp and weft aren’t generic inventory. Get the formula wrong and the mill wastes yarn. I sat with the client until the numbers matched the shop floor.

Tatkal Jobs (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Jobs, interviews, agencies — first Redux I actually understood, plus the animated About page. Frontend Engineer Tatkal Jobs — consultancy. Admin for jobs, interviews, students, agencies, employees, plus the public job site. I also made the About page infographics. This is where Redux stopped being a tutorial. Recruitment admin + job site. First time I really used Redux in production. Also built the animated About page. URL: https://www.tatkaljobs.com/ Tags: Job Portal, Recruitment, Admin Panel
Tatkal Jobs — Too many entities in one admin: Jobs, interviews, agencies, students, employees. Without a store that made sense, the UI fought itself.

FlightsTravel (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) UK flight booking site — tore out a filter loop that grew with every click and rewrote search results. Frontend Engineer FlightsTravel.co.uk (Flights & Travels Ltd) had a search UX that melted under filters. Legacy results page mixed branching and array-shaped filter state. A previous engineer spent about a month on it. I rebuilt the results layer and fixed the filter model. One filter click used to run 368 iterations and roughly double with each extra filter. After the rewrite: flat 33 — search stayed usable under real filter stacks. URL: https://www.flightstravel.co.uk/ Tags: Travel, Performance, Refactor
FlightsTravel — Filter loops that compound: First filter → ~368 iterations. Second → ~700. Third → ~1,300. Every click made the page slower.
FlightsTravel — Legacy results spaghetti: Filter options lived as selected arrays, so every change rescanned everything. Hard to fix without rewriting how selection was represented.

ZovilStore (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Phone and laptop cases you can customize — shop and admin in Next.js, Vercel + AWS. Full-Stack Engineer ZovilStore — pick a case, pick the options, see it. Storefront and admin in Next.js + Tailwind. Vercel for the site, AWS for the rest. Phone and laptop accessory shop with live customization, plus an admin. Next.js on Vercel, APIs on AWS. Tags: E-commerce, Customization, Admin Panel
ZovilStore — See it before you buy it: Accessory options had to update on the product, not after a refresh.

Thomas Cook Admin Panel (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Thomas Cook ops admin — I wrote the calendar because nothing off the shelf did overlaps and ranges. Frontend Engineer Internal ops panel for Thomas Cook: who is on which tour, when they’re free. The calendar had to show overlapping events and let you pick ranges. Off-the-shelf widgets couldn’t. Internal Thomas Cook admin. The calendar — overlapping tours, date ranges — didn’t exist in a library, so I wrote it. Tags: Travel, Admin Panel, Calendar
Thomas Cook Admin Panel — The calendar was the job: Overlapping events and range select at the same time. Every library we tried failed one of those.

Implr (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) A StringERP module we pulled out and shipped as its own product. Lead Engineer Implr started as a folder inside StringERP. It was useful on its own, so I pulled it out — own API, own pipeline — without breaking the ERP. Took a StringERP module, cut the shared bits, gave it its own deploy. StringERP kept working. Tags: Micro-Service, SaaS, Product Launch
Implr — Cut it out without the ERP falling over: Shared code, shared assumptions. Needed a real boundary and a contract, not a copy-paste of the folder.

Gatflix (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) GATE coaching — chunked lecture uploads, streams that don’t leak the file URL, Express SSR. Frontend Engineer Gatflix — GATE coaching: live classes, lectures, tests. I was on it for 6+ months. Videos were huge and people tried to steal them. Next.js SSR wasn’t a given yet, so we compiled React and served HTML from Express. Six months on a GATE coaching site: chunked video uploads, streams that didn’t leak the file URL, and SSR the hard way — compile React to JS, serve it with Express. Tags: EdTech, Video, SSR, Security
Gatflix — Don’t leak the video URL: Lectures had to play without a URL you could paste into another tab, and without a download button that actually worked.
Gatflix — Files that don’t fit in one request: A single PUT of a lecture would die. Chunk it, resume it.
Gatflix — SSR without a framework for it: SEO wanted HTML. We compiled the React app to vanilla JS and let Express serve it.

Magic Author (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) An eBook creation platform — my first React project, and the hardest one I ever shipped. Frontend Developer Magic Author is a platform where users can create eBooks on the go. It was my very first React project. The core engineering challenge was the BookShelf module, where authors design book covers using canvas-based tools (Fabric.js) and write content in any language. I had no prior knowledge of web storage, the Canvas API, or Fabric.js — and the existing codebase was messy. Despite that, I shipped it. Shipped my first React project — a complex canvas-based eBook creation platform — despite having no prior experience with web storage, Canvas API, or Fabric.js. Tags: eBooks, Canvas, Creative Tools

Magic Author — Canvas & Fabric.js — Zero Prior Experience: The BookShelf book-cover designer relied on Fabric.js and the Canvas API, neither of which I had encountered before. Learning both while debugging a problematic existing codebase was the hardest challenge of my early career.
Magic Author — Web Storage: Persisting user eBook state across sessions required understanding and implementing browser web storage, also new to me at the time.

Laahchee Marketing site with GSAP timelines — Next.js 15, React 19, keep it at 60fps. Frontend Engineer Laahchee is a marketing site that lives or dies on motion. Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind v4, GSAP timelines on scroll. If it dropped frames, it wasn’t done. Scroll-driven GSAP timelines that stay at 60fps. Next.js 15 / React 19, not a slideshow that janks on a phone. Tags: Frontend, Animation, Web, Performance
Laahchee — Motion vs the main thread: Lots of scroll-triggered timelines. Easy to thrash layout. Had to keep 60fps.
Laahchee — GSAP + React 19: Client animations next to server components. Don’t fight the new React, don’t freeze the page.

Jivita Design Next.js storefront — SSR for SEO, Mongo behind it, Tailwind + Alpine for the bits that need to move. Full-Stack Engineer Jivita is a Next.js storefront. SSR for product pages, Mongo for data, Tailwind for layout, Alpine.js for the small client bits. Shopping pages that load as HTML, not a spinner. Storefront that search engines can actually index. Interactivity stayed on Alpine so Next didn’t ship a SPA to shop. Tags: E-commerce, Full-Stack, UI/UX
Jivita Design — SSR vs clicky UI: Needed product pages as HTML. Also needed hover, drawers, small interactions. Alpine, not a second React tree.
Jivita Design — Mongo without waiting: Catalog from Mongo. Don’t make the first paint wait on a fat client fetch.

DS Universe Scroll site with Lenis + GSAP — Next.js 16, React 19, motion tied to the wheel. Frontend Engineer DS Universe is a scroll-driven marketing site. Next.js 16, React 19, Lenis for momentum scroll, GSAP for the scenes. If the animation doesn’t match the scroll, it’s wrong. Lenis scroll + GSAP ScrollTrigger so scenes fire on the wheel, not on a timer. Works on a phone, not just a 27-inch demo. Tags: Creative Web, Animation, Immersive
DS Universe — Scroll has to match the scene: Different screens, different refresh rates. ScrollTrigger and Lenis had to stay in lockstep.

Creg Caribbean (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Caribbean listings on a Mapbox map — React, Redux, Ant Design for the dashboard. Frontend Engineer Creg Caribbean is a listings product for the Caribbean. Mapbox-GL is the search. React + Redux hold pins and filters. Ant Design is the back-office for the listings themselves. Listings live on the map, not in a table you scroll forever. Hundreds of pins, Redux keeps filters and the map in the same state. Tags: Real Estate, Maps, Dashboard
Creg Caribbean — Too many pins: Mapbox + React will stall if you dump every listing as a React node. Pins had to stay in the map layer.

Gateflix (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) GATE video courses — HLS.js so lectures adapt to the network, Redux for progress. Frontend Engineer Gateflix is GATE coaching in a browser. Video is the product. HLS.js for adaptive bitrate, Redux for courses and progress, a rich editor for notes. Lectures stream as HLS, not a single MP4 that buffers on a 3G train. Progress and catalogs live in Redux. Tags: EdTech, Video Streaming, Platform
Gateflix — Video on bad networks: Students weren’t all on office wifi. A single MP4 meant a spinner. HLS had to pick a bitrate that fit.

HK Analytics (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Analytics dashboard — AG-Grid for the tables, Highcharts for the graphs, Next.js around it. Frontend Engineer HK Analytics is a dashboard for people who live in tables. Next.js + Tailwind. AG-Grid for the grids. Highcharts for the charts. If you dump 10k rows into a <table>, the browser dies. We didn’t. Thousands of rows without locking the tab. AG-Grid virtualizes the table; Highcharts only redraws when the data actually changed. Tags: Data Analytics, Dashboard, Enterprise
HK Analytics — Too many rows: Thousands of rows plus charts. A naive table froze the tab. Charts re-rendering on every parent update made it worse.

RK Synthetics B2B corporate site — Next.js 15 server components, less JS on the wire. Frontend Engineer RK Synthetics is a B2B company site. Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind v4, Turbopack in dev. Server components first so the marketing pages aren’t a 400kb SPA. Corporate pages as server components. Smaller JS, faster first paint, search engines get HTML. Tags: Corporate Website, B2B, Performance
RK Synthetics — Old content, new stack: Legacy pages into TypeScript + server components. Don’t ship a client bundle for a brochure.

Sequelis Marketing site where GSAP timelines react to scroll and hover — Next.js 15. Frontend Engineer Sequelis is a marketing site that sells with motion. Next.js 15, React 19, GSAP timelines on scroll and hover. If it only worked on a desktop, it wasn’t shipped. GSAP timelines that fire on scroll and hover. Same motion on a phone as on a desktop — scaled, not stripped. Tags: Creative Web, Interactive, Frontend
Sequelis — Motion on a phone: Timelines that look fine on a 27-inch screen will hitch on a mid-range Android. Had to test both.

@knovator/can (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) npm package — `<Can>` and `hasAccessOf` so admin UIs stop sprinkling role ifs. Open Source Creator Admin panels have roles. We were writing the same ifs on every button. `@knovator/can` is a small npm package: `hasAccessOf` / `hasAccessTo` for logic, a `<Can>` component for JSX. One permission shape. Admin screens stopped growing a forest of `role ===`. One permission object, a `<Can>` wrap, done. URL: https://github.com/knovator/Can Tags: NPM Package, Open Source, Access Control
@knovator/can — Ifs everywhere: Every action had its own role check. Miss one and a button shows up for the wrong person.

@knovator/api (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Axios wrapper — one `setAPIConfig`, tokens and cancel-in-flight live there. Open Source Creator `@knovator/api` wraps Axios. `setAPIConfig` once — base URL, token, errors. `fetchUrl` for the call. If you fire the same endpoint twice, the first one cancels. One config for base URL, token, errors. Duplicate in-flight calls cancel. Less copy-paste Axios in every screen. URL: https://github.com/knovator/api Tags: NPM Package, Open Source, API Wrapper
@knovator/api — Token on every call: Every screen was passing the token and the base URL. Easy to miss. Easy to double-fetch.

Game Design Platform React 18 UI for a game-design tool — Tailwind, actually usable on a phone. Frontend Engineer Frontend for a game-design tool. React 18, Tailwind. The hard part wasn’t the look — it was keeping editors and palettes usable when the screen is 375px. Design tools that still work on a phone. Tailwind breakpoints, not a hidden desktop-only canvas. Tags: Interactive UI, Responsive, Platform
Game Design Platform — Editors on a phone: Design UIs assume a mouse and a wide canvas. Had to collapse tools without losing the actual job.

Digibooks (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Digital books — Draft.js for authoring, HLS.js so video isn’t a downloadable MP4. Frontend Engineer Digibooks is a reading product. React + Redux on the frontend. I owned the hard modules: a real editor, video that isn’t a stealable file, and live sync. Authors get Draft.js. Readers get HLS chunks, not an MP4 URL. Firebase keeps sessions in sync. Tags: EdTech, Digital Publishing, SSR
Digibooks — Books aren’t a textarea: Authors needed formatting, embeds, structure. A contenteditable with hope wasn’t going to ship.
Digibooks — Don’t leak the video: Premium lectures inside books. A direct MP4 is a download. Chunk it.

Digibooks Admin Panel (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Digibooks CMS — React, Redux, Ant Design. Fine Uploader so a 2GB lecture doesn’t time out. Frontend Engineer Back office for Digibooks. React, Redux, Ant Design. Users, books, configs. The painful part was video: a single POST of a lecture file would time out. Ops upload lectures in chunks. If the wifi dies at 80%, they resume — they don’t start over. Tags: Admin Panel, CMS
Digibooks Admin Panel — Huge files: Lectures and PDFs are big. A naive upload dies halfway. Need chunks and a resume.

Gateflix Admin Panel (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Gateflix CMS — same Ant Design stack as Digibooks admin, courses and video assets. Frontend Engineer Admin for Gateflix — courses, students, video. Same React / Redux / Ant Design shape as Digibooks admin. That’s the point: two products, one way to build a table. Ops manage courses and video from one panel. Same Ant Design patterns as Digibooks, so we weren’t inventing a second admin language. Tags: EdTech, Admin Panel
Gateflix Admin Panel — Don’t fork the admin: A second custom table kit would have doubled the bugs. Reuse the Digibooks patterns.

Stay Classy (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Shop with Next.js SSR — product pages as HTML, zoom and sliders on top. Frontend Engineer Stay Classy is a shop. SPA product pages weren’t showing up in search and first paint was a spinner. Next.js SSR for the pages. Zoom, sliders, and cart still on the client. Product pages as HTML. Google can index them. Shoppers don’t wait on a blank SPA. Tags: E-commerce, SSR, Web Platform
Stay Classy — SPA vs search: Client-rendered product pages were invisible to crawlers and slow on a cheap phone.

WonderMD Patient Portal (Knovator Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) Patient portal — OpenTok in the browser, Stripe for the visit, Next.js + Tailwind. Frontend Engineer WonderMD is telehealth. I built the patient portal in Next.js and Tailwind — book, pay, sit in the call. History and appointments in the same app. Visit happens in the tab. OpenTok for video, Stripe for the bill.
